  1. 1 Must see within Upper Serangoon · Wok noodles

    Ah Hock Fried Hokkien Mee

    A Michelin Plate stall and Chomp Chomp's most famous name — thick yellow noodles and bee hoon fried with prawns and squid in a prawn stock simmered for hours, finished with a dollop of sambal. The go-to plate at Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by , , +1,

  2. 2 Must see within Upper Serangoon

    Ming Fa Duck Rice

    One of Singapore's best Teochew braised duck rice stalls, tucked in Hougang's Hainanese Village Centre (Lorong Ah Soo). Tender lean duck over yam rice, drenched in a mildly sweet-savoury five-spice sauce, with an anchovy-loaded sambal. Opens at dawn and usually sells out by early lunch.

    Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-01, Singapore 530105

    Recommended by , , +1,

  3. 3 Must see within Upper Serangoon · Wok noodles

    Hougang Oyster Omelette & Fried Kway Teow

    A 30-year Hougang heritage stall run by Mr and Mrs Ong that still fries its oyster omelette in pork lard, with big juicy oysters and a fragrant char kway teow alongside. One of the island's best-rated orh luak, worth the queue.

    Blk 435A Hougang Avenue 8, Singapore 531435

    Recommended by , , +1,

  4. 4 Must see within Upper Serangoon

    Hougang Tou Mu Kung (Kew Ong Yah Temple)

    Singapore's oldest temple dedicated to the Nine Emperor Gods (Kew Ong Yah), completed 1921 and gazetted a National Monument on 14 Jan 2005. Its blend of Hokkien and later Teochew roof forms anchors Hougang's Teochew heritage, and it remains the focus of the annual Nine Emperor Gods Festival.

    Look for Free entry; busiest during the ninth-lunar-month festival

    779A Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore

    Recommended by , ,

  5. 5 Must see within Upper Serangoon

    Kampong Lorong Buangkok

    Singapore's last surviving mainland village, established in 1956 when traditional-medicine seller Sng Teow Koon bought the swampy land and rented plots to Malay and Chinese families. A cluster of zinc-roofed houses on dirt tracks around a surau, in the Trafalgar (Buangkok) subzone of Hougang; Ms Sng Mui Hong, the founder's youngest daughter, still lives here as landlord. Old four-digit street signs survive.

    Look for Free; a living village — visit respectfully, don't enter homes

    7 Lorong Buangkok (off Gerald Drive, via Buangkok Crescent), Singapore 547557

    Recommended by , ,

  6. 6 Must see within Upper Serangoon · Malay & nasi Padang

    Chomp Chomp Satay

    One of two Chomp Chomp stalls listed in the MICHELIN Guide with a Michelin Plate — skewers grilled over charcoal to order, a supper-time institution best eaten late at Serangoon Gardens with a plate of BBQ chicken wings alongside.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by , ,

  7. 7 Must see within Upper Serangoon · Malay & nasi Padang

    Aliff Nasi Lemak

    The most-recommended stall in the market — a Muslim-owned nasi lemak (from S$3) built on freshly squeezed coconut milk, pandan-scented rice and a shiok sambal, with crisp ikan bilis and add-ons. Serangoon Gardens' daytime counterpoint to Chomp Chomp.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by , ,

  8. 8 Must see within Upper Serangoon · Wok noodles

    Original Simon Road Hokkien Mee

    Third- and fourth-generation hawkers who have fried their wet-style Hokkien mee to the same recipe since 1960 — whole prawns, squid rings and pork belly over noodles and bee hoon fried dry so they drink up a prawn-head-and-pork-rib stock, with free-flow crispy lard. Named for its old Simon Road home, now relocated to Kovan 209.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, #01-66, Singapore 530209

    Recommended by , ,

  9. 9 Must see within Upper Serangoon · Hawker & zi char

    Anshun Seafood Soup

    Widely cited as Singapore's best-rated fish soup — a clean, refined broth from a couple who started at Zion Road Blk 91 in 2002 before landing under a quiet Hougang coffeeshop. The 'hei bai' bowl of fried and sliced fish together, done with milk, is the order.

    174C Hougang Avenue 1, Singapore 533174

    Recommended by , ,

  10. 10 Must see within Upper Serangoon

    Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary

    A National Monument (gazetted 14 Jan 2005) and the historic heart of Serangoon's Teochew Catholic community, which was mostly farmers in the 19th century. The present Gothic church — pointed arches, a soaring nave — was blessed on 8 Dec 1901 and restored in 2019; the mission dates to pioneer priest Fr Ambrose Maistre in 1852.

    Look for Free entry; a stop on the Hougang Heritage Trail

    1259 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534795

    Recommended by ,

  11. 11 Must see within Upper Serangoon

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre

    Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre, open since 1972 with around 36 stalls. A night-time institution for BBQ stingray and sotong, Hokkien mee, satay, satay bee hoon, orh luak and charcoal chicken wings — as much a neighbourhood landmark as an eating spot.

    Look for Evenings to late night; busiest for supper

    20 Kensington Park Road, Singapore 557269

    Recommended by ,

  12. 12 Must see within Upper Serangoon · Malay & nasi Padang

    Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang

    A MICHELIN Guide-listed stall that pairs fragrant coconut rice with Ayam Taliwang, the fiery Lombok-style grilled chicken — the smoky, chilli-slicked bird against the cool creamy rice. The Ci Yuan branch of a beloved north-east name, right in Hougang.

    Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-40, Singapore 538776

    Recommended by ,

  13. 13 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Hawker & zi char

    Sin Heng Kee Porridge

    A Hougang corner-stall congee institution with a perpetual 30-minute queue — thick, hearty bowls of smooth Cantonese-style porridge piled with generous ingredients, warming Hougang residents for decades.

    685 Hougang Street 61, #01-150, S530685

    Recommended by , , +1,

  14. 14 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon

    Chee Tong Temple

    Completed in 1987 and designed by Tay Kheng Soon of Akitek Tenggara, this is widely regarded as Singapore's first truly modernist Chinese temple — its roof rising in eight-sided prisms that evoke a lotus, its corners deliberately kept un-sharp on the deities' guidance. A Hougang Heritage Trail 'Architectural Gem' and a documented modern-movement building.

    Look for Active temple; open daytime

    62 Hougang Avenue 3, Singapore 538844

    Recommended by , ,

  15. 15 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Hawker & zi char

    Chomp Chomp Fried Oyster

    The standout orh luak of Chomp Chomp — eggs and starch fried until charred and crisp at the edges around plump, briny oysters, drizzled with tangy chilli. A perennial pick across the centre's food-guide round-ups.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by , ,

  16. 16 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Hawker & zi char

    Good Luck BBQ Chicken Wings

    Chicken wings are practically Chomp Chomp's mascot, and Good Luck (Stall 29) grills some of the most sought-after — burnished, charred-edged skin over juicy meat, at roughly S$1.30 a wing. A supper staple of the Serangoon Gardens crowd.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-29, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by , ,

  17. 17 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Hawker & zi char

    Hai Wei Yuan BBQ

    Chomp Chomp's best sambal BBQ seafood — fresh, flaky stingray blanketed in an addictive sambal and grilled on a banana leaf (from S$12 for a small), plus BBQ sotong and cockles. A late-night favourite that draws its own queue.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by , ,

  18. 18 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Hawker & zi char

    Ang Sar Lee Satay Bee Hoon

    A 40-plus-year Chomp Chomp veteran plating thin bee hoon drowned in a fragrant satay peanut gravy with cuttlefish, prawns, pork and tau pok — the Serangoon Gardens rendition of a dish few hawkers still make well.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by , ,

  19. 19 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon

    Ah Seng Braised Duck Rice

    Rated among Singapore's best Teochew braised duck — tender, herbal braised duck over rice (from S$4) with pig's stomach soup and offal, from a decades-old recipe. Queues form before it opens.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-44, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by , ,

  20. 20 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon

    Serangoon Garden Bakery & Confectionery

    A 40-year neighbourhood bakery baking from 2am — classic coconut, cream-puff, chicken-sausage and curry buns from S$1.10, all made from scratch. A generational fixture inside the market.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-45/46, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by , ,

  21. 21 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon

    Fatt Soon Kueh

    A decades-old stall hand-making Teochew kueh — soon kueh, png kueh and gu chye kueh at around S$1 each, using only fresh fillings. A Kovan 209 heritage name.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-17, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by , ,

  22. 22 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Hainanese chicken rice

    Hougang Hainanese Curry Rice

    The lunch-hour queue of Kovan 209 — a heaped plate of Hainanese-style chye png flooded with curry, braise and pork gravies, with fried pork chop and cabbage. Old-school comfort food.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-25, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by , ,

  23. 23 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Hainanese chicken rice

    Pow Sing Restaurant

    A Serangoon Gardens institution since 1983 — the Hainanese founders opened a chicken rice stall, then hired a Nonya chef, and today it is rated among Singapore's best traditional Hainanese chicken rice with a Peranakan zi char spread.

    59 Serangoon Garden Way, S555955

    Recommended by , ,

  24. 24 Worth the detour within Upper Serangoon · Cafés & modern

    Apollo Coffee Bar

    A long-running Serangoon Gardens cafe from the Atlas Coffeehouse / Columbus Coffee team — minimalist interiors, a solid brunch menu and a cult dark-chocolate-and-miso-caramel softserve. The area's flagship specialty-coffee address.

    65 Serangoon Garden Way, S555961
